title: User Guide Surface
markdown:
The `/guide` page is a **plain-language overview of every user-facing feature** — "what it is, what it does, how to use it" — aimed at non-engineers. It is deliberately kept separate from this technical reference: Architecture explains how the system is built; the User Guide explains what each feature does for you.

It is reached from a **tile on the Settings hub** (`ADVANCED_ITEMS` in `navConfig.ts`), not the day-to-day nav.

**Served exactly like this page.** Each section is static, hand-authored JSON shipped in the image — `packages/core/openexecutive/guide/prebuilt/<id>.json`, one file per entry in `guide/sections.py` → `GUIDE_SECTIONS`. The route `api/routes/guide.py` exposes `GET /guide/sections` and `GET /guide/sections/{id}`, mirroring the architecture routes. **Nothing on the serving path calls an LLM.**

**Shared loader.** Both surfaces load their files through one class — `openexecutive.utils.prebuilt_store.PrebuiltDocStore` — pointed at each module's own `prebuilt/` directory. The same fields apply (`section_id`, `title`, `markdown`, `mermaid`, `generated_at`), and the same path-traversal guard rejects any id containing a separator or dot segment.

**Shared renderer.** The UI reuses the architecture page's `DynamicSection` component via a `basePath` prop (`"architecture"` by default, `"guide"` for the guide), so deep links, lazy loading, and Markdown sanitization behave identically. The guide is intentionally diagram-free — its sections carry `mermaid: null`.

**Keeping it current:** when a user-facing feature is added or materially changed, add or update the matching `guide/prebuilt/<id>.json` (and its registry entry in `guide/sections.py` + the mirror list in `app/guide/page.tsx`), the same way technical sections are maintained here. Every section must include a `**How to use:**` walkthrough (and an `**Example:**` where one helps) — `tests/unit/test_guide_prebuilt.py` enforces it. Because Ask OE inlines the current page's section into its user turn, those steps also ground its "how do I…" answers.
